item.title: Trump claims Iran gave US an energy 'present' tied to Hormuz
item.description:
President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that Iran had made a major energy-related concession to the United States, describing it as a gift that "arrived today" — though he offered no specifics and Iran has repeatedly denied engaging in any negotiations with Washington.

"They gave us a present and the present arrived today, and it was a very big present, worth a tremendous amount of money," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office, according to Reuters. "It wasn't nuclear; it was oil-and-gas-related, and it was a very nice thing they did."

Trump said the gesture was connected to the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil supply passes. He characterized it as proof that "we're dealing with the right people" in Tehran and claimed Iran had also agreed it "will never have a nuclear weapon," The Independent reported.

item.title: Netanyahu taps top aide Dermer to vet US-Iran deal
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu assigned his closest confidant, former Strategic Affairs Minister Ron Dermer, to monitor US-Iranian negotiations and ensure Israel's core interests are not sacrificed in any potential deal to end the war, according to Bloomberg, citing an Israeli official speaking on condition of anonymity.

Dermer's primary focus is on ensuring the dismantlement of Iran's nuclear program and the removal and elimination of roughly 440 kilograms of highly enriched uranium — material that Iran reportedly boasted to White House Special Envoy Steve Witkoff was sufficient for 11 nuclear bombs, according to Jewish Insider.

item.title: US airstrikes kill 15 Iraq PMF fighters, including Anbar commander
item.description:
Airstrikes attributed to the United States and Israel killed at least 15 fighters from Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces and wounded 30 others in western Iraq early Tuesday, in the deadliest single attack on the Iran-backed militia coalition since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February.

The strikes hit a PMF command headquarters in Iraq's Anbar province during a security meeting attended by senior commanders, according to Reuters. Among the dead was Saad al-Baiji, the PMF's operations commander for Anbar province. The PMF confirmed his death along with 14 of his companions in a statement posted on social media, calling the attack "a treacherous American targeting that struck the operations headquarters".

item.title: Iran charges ships up to $2M for Hormuz passage
item.description:
Iran has begun levying transit fees of up to $2 million per voyage on some commercial vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, effectively creating an informal toll on the world's most critical maritime energy chokepoint, according to Bloomberg.

The payments are being sought on an ad hoc basis and do not appear to be systematic, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. Some ships have already made the payment, though the mechanism and currency used remain unclear. Iranian authorities have officially denied that a formal policy exists, calling the reports "unfounded".

item.title: Israeli airstrike hits Christian town north of Beirut for first time
item.description:
An Israeli airstrike struck the Christian town of Sahel Alma north of Beirut on Tuesday, marking the first time the area had been targeted in the expanding war between Israel and Hezbollah, according to Lebanese state media and Reuters. There were no immediate reports of casualties, but witnesses told Reuters they heard several blasts and saw white smoke rising from the town.

The strike represents a widening of Israel's air campaign into areas previously untouched by the conflict, which has killed more than 1,000 people in Lebanon and displaced over one million since fighting escalated on March 2.

item.title: Oil drops as US sends Iran 15-point ceasefire proposal
item.description: Oil prices swung sharply on Monday and Tuesday as reports emerged that the United States had sent Iran a 15-point proposal to end the war now in its fourth week, offering a potential off-ramp from a conflict that has roiled global energy markets and sent American gas prices soaring.

item.title: Brazil court places Bolsonaro under house arrest on health grounds
item.description:
Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ruled on Tuesday to place former President Jair Bolsonaro under house arrest on health grounds, reversing months of denied requests from the right-wing leader's legal team, according to Reuters.

Bolsonaro, 71, has been serving a 27-year prison sentence since November for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. The house arrest will last for an initial 90-day period, after which Moraes said conditions will be reassessed. "The presence of the requirements necessary for maintaining humanitarian house arrest will be reassessed, including a medical examination if needed," the justice wrote in the decision.

item.title: Astronomers spot two planets forming around a young star like our sun
item.description: An international team of astronomers has confirmed the discovery of a second planet forming in the dust disk surrounding the young star WISPIT 2, making it only the second known system where two planets have been directly observed taking shape around their host star. The findings, published Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, offer what researchers describe as the closest analog yet to our own solar system in its infancy.

item.title: Trump sends 15-point peace plan to Iran as Hormuz opens to some ships
item.description: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that he had sent a peace plan to Iran and expressed optimism about ending nearly a month of war, as Tehran informed the United Nations it would permit "non-hostile" vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz — a narrow waterway through which roughly one-fifth of global oil normally flows.

item.title: NASA confirms Artemis II is go for April 1 moon launch
item.description:
Four astronauts are one week away from becoming the first humans to travel to the moon in more than half a century. NASA is targeting April 1 for the launch of Artemis 2, a 10-day test flight that will send a crew around the far side of the moon and back aboard the Orion spacecraft atop the Space Launch System rocket.

The crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialist Christina Koch from NASA, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen — entered quarantine in Houston on March 18 and will fly to Kennedy Space Center roughly five days before launch. The mission will make Glover the first person of color, Koch the first woman, and Hansen the first non-American to travel to the moon.

item.title: Iran mocks US ceasefire plan, says Americans 'negotiating with yourselves'
item.description:
President Trump's assertion that the United States is engaged in productive negotiations with Iran to end the month-old war has been met with open derision from Tehran, where an Iranian military spokesperson on Wednesday said the Americans "are negotiating with yourselves."

Lt. Col. Ebrahim Zolfaghari, speaking in a prerecorded video on Iranian state television, dismissed Trump's diplomatic overtures. "Don't dress up your defeat as an agreement. Your era of empty promises has come to an end," he said, according to the Associated Press. His remarks came shortly after the Trump administration delivered a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran through Pakistani intermediaries.

item.title: Iran dismisses US 15-point ceasefire plan as war nears one-month mark
item.description: Iran on Wednesday dismissed an American proposal to end the nearly month-old war, with a military spokesman declaring that Tehran will "never come to terms" with Washington, even as the Trump administration insisted that productive negotiations were underway.

item.title: AI detects landslide risks years in advance using satellite radar data
item.description:
Around the village of Kimtang in central Nepal, cracks run through concrete steps and trees grow at odd angles — signs that the ground is shifting beneath residents' feet. Scientists at the University of Melbourne have used artificial intelligence to analyze satellite radar data and confirm what villagers long suspected: their homes sit atop an unstable slope at high risk of a devastating landslide. The AI marked the danger zone in bright red on a color map, a warning that could prove lifesaving.

The Nepal project is part of a growing wave of research applying AI to one of the world's most destructive and difficult-to-predict natural hazards. In the first two months of 2026 alone, 91 fatal landslides killed more than 800 people worldwide, according to data tracked by Eos. Researchers across multiple continents are now racing to deploy machine learning systems that can detect the subtle ground movements that precede catastrophic slope failures.

item.title: Gold surges as oil slump eases inflation fears
item.description:
Gold prices climbed sharply on Wednesday as a steep decline in oil prices eased inflation concerns and tempered expectations for interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, even as mixed signals over a potential U.S.-Iran ceasefire kept markets on edge.

Spot gold rose nearly 2% to around $4,551 per ounce, while gold futures for April delivery jumped more than 3%, according to CNBC. The rally came as oil prices sank more than 5% on optimism that Washington was pursuing a diplomatic path to pause the conflict, with Brent crude falling to roughly $99 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate dropping to around $88.

item.title: Global stocks surge as US sends 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran
item.description:
Stock markets around the world rallied on Wednesday as investors reacted to reports that the United States had delivered a 15-point ceasefire proposal to Iran, raising hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the nearly month-old conflict that has roiled global markets and sent energy prices soaring.

The S&P 500 rose 1.1% in early trading, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed more than 500 points and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.3%, according to the Associated Press. In Europe, Germany's DAX advanced 1.7%, France's CAC 40 climbed 1.4%, and Britain's FTSE 100 rose 0.9%. Asian markets posted even sharper gains, with Japan's Nikkei 225 surging nearly 3% and South Korea's Kospi jumping more than 3%. Oil prices fell sharply, with Brent crude dropping more than 5%.

item.title: NASA to send water-hunting tool to Moon aboard JAXA-ISRO rover
item.description: NASA announced it will provide a water-detecting instrument to the Lunar Polar Exploration mission, a joint effort by JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) and ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) that aims to land a rover at the Moon's south pole no earlier than 2028.

item.title: Trump sets May 14-15 for rescheduled Beijing summit with Xi
item.description:
President Donald Trump will travel to Beijing on May 14 and 15 for a rescheduled summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the White House announced Wednesday, setting firm dates for a trip that had been thrown into uncertainty by the ongoing U.S. and Israeli war against Iran.

The visit was originally planned for March 31 to April 2 but was postponed as Trump said he needed to remain in Washington to oversee military operations, known as Operation Epic Fury. The announcement comes even as the conflict in Iran continues and the administration presses Tehran to accept a ceasefire proposal.

item.title: Iran signals preference for Vance as US negotiator, rejecting Witkoff and Kushner
item.description:
Iran has signaled to the Trump administration that it prefers to negotiate with Vice President JD Vance rather than other senior officials, rejecting renewed engagement with special envoy Steve Witkoff and presidential son-in-law Jared Kushner, according to a CNN report citing two regional sources.

The message was conveyed through back channels to mediating countries, with Iranian representatives expressing that talks involving Witkoff and Kushner would not be productive given what sources described as a "deficit of trust". The collapse of earlier nuclear negotiations in Geneva, followed within days by US and Israeli military strikes that began on February 28, left Tehran deeply skeptical of the pair's intentions.

item.title: Iran rejects U.S. ceasefire plan, issues five demands
item.description: Iran on Wednesday dismissed a 15-point American proposal to end the nearly month-long war in the Middle East, with Tehran issuing its own set of demands and mocking Washington's diplomatic efforts as detached from reality. The rejection came as fighting between Iran on one side and the United States and Israel on the other showed no signs of abating.

item.title: U.N. report finds migratory freshwater fish declined 81% since 1970
item.description: Migratory freshwater fish populations have declined by 81 percent worldwide since 1970, according to a new United Nations assessment that calls the crisis one of the steepest drops recorded for any major vertebrate group. The report, released this week at the CMS COP15 wildlife conference in Campo Grande, Brazil, identifies 325 species in urgent need of coordinated international conservation action.
